messages:
alex_m: heads up — getting multiple customer escalations for hosted inference in eu-west. errors are 502/504 and some client timeouts. started ~10:12 UTC. rolling in support tickets. :(

maria_support: forwarded a customer's error dump: request_id=req_0a1b2c3d status=504, latency=30s, user impacted: fintech-prod. user says they saw this across 3 regions but mostly eu-west.

sara_ops: can you paste a sample request_id and a CURL repro? need to triage routing vs runtime.

maria_support: sample: req_0a1b2c3d. Customer repro curl attached: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — they got an immediate 502, then repeated 504s.

jamie_reliability: telemetry quick scan: surge of 502s at the edge proxy (apigw-eu-west) starting 10:11:40, p50 backend latency normal but p95 and tail spiking. spikes align with increased TLS handshake queue length on the loadbalancer. logs show upstream auth middleware returning 500s and triggering proxy circuit.

ingress-bot: [ALERT] apigw-eu-west TLS queue length > 800 (10:12:03). 5xx rate +120% over baseline.

olivia_engineer: i pulled proxy logs for req_0a1b2c3d — stack: `auth-mw -> billing-kv -> upstream-runtime`. auth-mw returns 500 when billing-kv GET /tenant/meters times out (500ms+) and auth.fallthrough set to fail. snippet: 
```
ERROR auth-mw: bill-kv timeout (500ms) tenant=acme corp request=req_0a1b2c3d
proxy: upstream circuit open -> returning 502
```

alex_m: so billing KV latency causes auth to fail open? that's surprising — auth should degrade to cached tokens, not 500. Did a recent deploy touch auth-mw?

deploybot: deploy 2026-03-15T09:58Z rolled auth-mw v2.3.1 to eu-west and ap-south. Rollout flagged no immediate errors.

jamie_reliability: v2.3.1 changed billing lookup to a synchronous remote call for metering (perf rationale), which reintroduces a network hop in the auth path. under TLS backlog it amplifies tail latency and leads to 5xx.

maria_support: customers want ETA and mitigation. asking for temporary workaround we can give them.

sara_ops: immediate mitigation options: 1) revert auth-mw change (slow, needs deploy) 2) hotfix auth-mw to use local cache fallback on billing-kv timeout (small patch) 3) route production traffic away from apigw-eu-west to other regions (manual routing) 4) open circuit in front of billing-kv to fail fast. thoughts?

olivia_engineer: we can flip the fallback flag in auth-mw config to allow cached tokens on billing timeout — config change, no code change. low risk.

jamie_reliability: suggested hotfix sequence: flip auth.fallback_to_cache=true, enable billing-kv circuitbreaker with 50ms timeout, scale up apigw TLS workers to drain handshake backlog.

alex_m: do it. priority: reduce customer 5xx ASAP. assign owners and ETA.

olivia_engineer: taking config flip and cb. doing change in eu-west now. i'll post CRO.

ingress-bot: [ACTION] runbook step executed: increase-apigw-workers triggered by olivia_engineer at 10:20 UTC.

olivia_engineer: config flipped and circuit enabled at 10:22 UTC. monitoring shows 502 rate dropped ~70% in 2m. posting metrics: apigw-5xx-rate down from 18% -> 5% p10.

maria_support: customer confirms reduction in errors. sending note: "we applied a temporary fallback to cached tokens while we investigate — monitoring ongoing". :thumbsup:

jamie_reliability: next steps: rollback the billing lookup change or implement async metering. short-term: revert billing lookup to background metric send within auth-mw so it doesn't block. long-term: add a local TTL'd meter cache and circuit-breaker with proper ejection.

alex_m: action items (owners):
- olivia_engineer: follow up telemetry + run security review on token cache fallback (due EOD)
- jamie_reliability: prototype async metering in auth-mw and PR by tomorrow 14:00 UTC
- deploybot/team: prepare canary revert for auth-mw v2.3.1 if needed (on-call)
- maria_support: customer comms templates and incident updates (ASAP)

olivia_engineer: quick note — toggling fallback increases risk surface (stale meter info). we should gate with a feature flag and timeline.

alex_m: agreed. schedule: keep fallback on until we ship async metering or revert. if errors rise again, we'll rollback.

maria_support: creating support ticket update now and pinging affected accounts.

jamie_reliability: postmortem checklist: record timeline, root cause = auth-mw synchronous billing lookup + TLS handshake backlog; mitigations = config fallback + billing circuit + scale workers; action items recorded above. i'll own the RCA writeup.

olivia_engineer: logs and config changes saved to incident/858001 (internal).

alex_m: closing war room for now — on-call keep monitoring for 2 hours and escalate if p50 > 2s or 5xx > 1% baseline. :eyes:

ingress-bot: [CLOSE] apigw-eu-west immediate mitigation stable at 10:55 UTC.
